title: Finite bounds on changes of mind

based_on.title: How to approximate fuzzy sets: mind-changes and the Ershov Hierarchy
based_on.pages: Article 55; section The Classical Ershov Hierarchy, Definition 3, Remark 1 and classical finite Boolean forms in Theorem 3

summary: Bound how often a computable membership guess may change, and track the bounds through complements, computable preimages and finite Boolean combinations.
abstract: A program can recognize a member of an enumerable set by changing its answer once, from no to yes. Allowing a fixed number of revisions gives a finer way to study computable guesses that eventually become correct. We require every guess to begin with no and count both kinds of revision. Under this convention, no revisions allow only the empty set, one allows exactly the enumerable sets, and two allow their differences. Delaying a complement by one stage preserves the initial convention at the cost of one additional revision, while unions and intersections can be handled by adding the two allowances. These rules give a finite budget for every finite Boolean combination of enumerable sets. Even one permitted change supplies no computable deadline for settling the answer: the halting problem already demonstrates the distinction.
